entries.title: Who runs payroll
entries.body: HCMs don't run payroll. Payroll runs payroll and signs off time cards. Your job is getting records and transactions right before the cutoff, checking time cards every week, chasing managers, and bringing errors you can't resolve to payroll.
entries.source: HCM Academy: The HCM's role in payroll

entries.title: The payroll calendar
entries.body: The payroll calendar is the source of truth, and which calendar applies depends on the worker. Exempt staff and faculty are paid monthly; the monthly HCM transaction cutoff is around the 18th, so a change approved after it pays the next month, with retro. Hourly (non-exempt) staff are paid biweekly or weekly. Each of those periods has a Retro Change Cutoff for backdated changes, then the HCM transaction cutoff (the Friday before the period ends), then time cards due at noon on the Monday after it ends. A transaction counts only once it is fully approved, so leave time for every approver. [SME] Confirm the cutoff time of day, the weekly calendar, and which worker groups are paid weekly.
entries.source: Vanderbilt 2026 Payroll Calendar; HCM Academy: The Shared Administrative Calendar; Compensation impacts on payroll processing

entries.title: Time card approval order
entries.body: Employees enter and approve their own time. Managers approve. Payroll signs off. After sign-off, an approval can't be removed until payroll removes the sign-off.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Review and approve time cards

entries.title: Who fixes a time card
entries.body: Entering time is the employee's job. Managers review their team's time, ask employees about anything unclear, and approve it. You check time cards weekly, point the manager to the problem, and help them fix it. If you enter a correction yourself, do it only with the manager's confirmation, and keep a record. [SME] Confirm where Vanderbilt expects that record to live.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Weekly time card check; UKG: Timecards, Time Off, and Schedules for Managers

entries.title: Open pay period: Save, don't Submit
entries.body: If you enter time for someone in an open pay period, Save. Submitting early means you must edit, update, and resubmit later.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Weekly time card check

entries.title: Non-exempt PTO increments
entries.body: Non-exempt PTO is entered in 4-hour increments.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Enter PTO for an employee

entries.title: Overtime for non-exempt staff
entries.body: Federal law requires paying non-exempt employees overtime for hours over 40 in a workweek, even if the overtime wasn't approved in advance. Not getting approval is a conduct issue for the manager to address, not a reason to change the time or withhold pay.
entries.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Fair Labor Standards Act

entries.title: Late manager approvals
entries.body: Remind the manager with the employee names, the pay period, and the deadline. If they can't approve in time, escalate to their backup approver or supervisor. Don't approve as the manager yourself. [SME] Confirm the backup approver rule.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Weekly time card check; [SME]

entries.title: Retroactive pay changes
entries.body: Use the effective date on the approved document, even when it is in the past. Payroll recalculates the periods already paid and pays the difference. A backdated change must be entered and approved by the Retro Change Cutoff, about two business days before the HCM transaction cutoff, to make this payroll; after that, the back pay waits for the next run. [SME] Confirm how a backdated change approved between the two cutoffs pays.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Change salary; The Shared Administrative Calendar; Compensation impacts on payroll processing

entries.title: Off-cycle payments
entries.body: Use an off-cycle payment when a transaction failed to pay through no fault of the employee or the HCM, such as a system error, and the request meets the criteria on the form. It takes two things: the corrected or resubmitted transaction in Oracle, and the off-cycle request form. Then tell payroll when the transaction will be approved. Payroll runs the payment; you request it. It is the only way exempt staff are paid outside the monthly payroll.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Request an off-cycle payment

entries.title: One-time payments: Amount or Net
entries.body: Payments outside base pay, such as a bonus or a stipend, go in Individual Compensation, not Change Salary. Amount is gross: use it for a payment stated before taxes, such as a sign-on bonus. Net is take-home: use it when the employee should receive an exact amount, and Oracle grosses it up to cover taxes. Date the payment the first day of the payroll month it should pay in; if that month's cutoff has passed, use the next month. Leave Process separately set to Yes unless payroll says otherwise.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Process grossed-up additional compensation; Add a one-time payment (such as a sign-on bonus)

entries.title: Staff supplements
entries.body: A staff supplement pays extra for extra duties over a period. It is recurring, so it pays every payroll until its end date. If nobody knows when the duties end, leave it Ongoing and set yourself a reminder to end it. Ask your finance partner which supplement plan to use. Supplements are for staff; faculty, post-docs, students, and temps have their own.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Add a staff supplement

entries.title: Person, work relationship, assignment
entries.body: A person has one or more work relationships, and each holds one or more assignments. The assignment is where the job, position, department, manager, hours, and payroll live. Someone with two jobs has two assignments, each with its own manager. Check which assignment you are on before you act.
entries.source: HCM Academy: HCM Structure and Key Concepts

entries.title: Protecting employee data
entries.body: Your access is for your job, not for curiosity or favors. Keep personal data in Oracle, and download, print, or email it only when the task truly needs it. Never put SSNs in email, spreadsheets, file names, or tickets; identify people by person number. Share only what the task needs, with people who have a business need, and report a suspected incident right away [SME: where to report, and the approved way to share files].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Confidentiality and Secure Access Agreement (annual)

entries.title: Building a new analysis
entries.body: Build a new analysis only when no catalog or Departmental Playbook report fits. Pick the subject area, add only the columns you need, add filters, and spot-check the results against records you know. Hiding a column is not security, so leave out what you don't need. Save it in My Folders [SME: which reporting roles HCMs have].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Reporting 301

entries.title: Approvals and the notifications bell
entries.body: Most transactions route to approvers and are not final until every approver acts. The notifications bell shows each transaction's approval history: who approved, who it is waiting on, and any comments. Check it daily and before every cutoff. While approval is in progress, the requester can withdraw a transaction, fix it, and resubmit; the approvals then start over [SME: approval chains by transaction type].
entries.source: HCM Academy: HCM Workflow and Worklists

entries.title: Bad data in, bad data out
entries.body: One record feeds the next: the position feeds the requisition, conversion builds the assignment, and the assignment drives pay, costing, and every report. Read each field against the source document before you submit, fix errors while they are still pending, and never create a new record for someone already in progress. Fixes after payroll runs become retro adjustments in a later payroll.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Data integrity: bad data in, bad data out

entries.title: Reports show the date you ask for
entries.body: Oracle data is date effective. Set a report's as-of date to the date you care about: a hire or change that starts later will not show on a report run as of today. Pick only the prompt values you need, and spot-check results against Employment Info before you share them. A report only shows what is in Oracle.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Reporting 101

entries.title: Saving and exporting reports
entries.body: If you change a shared report, use Save As to keep your copy in My Folders, where only you can see it. Never save over the shared original. Your copy does not pick up later fixes to the original. Exports hold personal data, so store and share them only as policy allows [SME: rules for storing and emailing exported HR data].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Reporting 201

entries.title: FERPA and student information
entries.body: Once a student is in college, FERPA rights belong to the student. Education records, such as class schedules and grades, are shared only with the student's written consent or under a FERPA exception. Records about a student who works because they are a student are generally education records too. Do not confirm schedules, grades, or enrollment details to callers, parents, or outside employers; decline and refer the request [SME: which office handles these requests].
entries.source: HCM Academy: FERPA Tutorial for Staff

entries.title: Filing a document record
entries.body: Final, signed documents go on the employee's Oracle file as Document Records. Pick the Document Type that matches the document (a pay increase letter is Compensation Letters), name it the way the type's description shows, set Issued On to the date the document was presented to the employee, and attach only the final signed copy. Ask your HR consultant if you are unsure of the type.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Add a document record

entries.title: I-9 timing for a new hire
entries.body: Every paid employee needs a Form I-9, and staff and faculty also need a cleared background check before they start. The employee completes Section 1 no later than the first day of work for pay. The employer reviews the employee's documents and completes Section 2 within 3 business days of the first day [SME: who completes Section 2 at Vanderbilt, and in which system].
entries.source: HCM Academy: I-9 and background check requirements by worker type

entries.title: Find the right person first
entries.body: Search by person number, not by name or SSN, and check the person type and status before you select. Read the assignment and its history in Employment Info, including any future-dated change, before you start a transaction. A missing quick action usually means a security role issue, not a system error.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Quick Actions and Viewing Person and Employment Information

entries.title: Employee or contractor
entries.body: The facts of the work decide whether someone is an employee, not a contract, a label, or what anyone prefers. If the office directs how, when, and where the work is done, or supplies the tools, that points to employment. Students who perform services are generally employees. Settle the question before any work starts [SME: the contact for classification questions; the draft uses your EC].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Employee or independent contractor?

entries.title: Start with the Departmental Playbook
entries.body: For a check across your area, start with existing reports. The Departmental Playbook's costing reports (HCM Assignment Cost Allocation Plan, HCM Element Cost Allocation Plan, and HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan) confirm costing for your people. Reports show only the people your security allows, so two people can see different rows [SME: where the Playbook lives in the catalog].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Introduction to BI Reporting and the Departmental Playbook

entries.title: Clear to start, then convert
entries.body: No one starts work until PCB sends the clear to start email and the HCM converts the pending worker. Until then there is no hire record, no time card, and no pay. There is no unpaid trial or shadow day: work done for the office is paid work. Federal law requires I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work and Section 2 within 3 business days of it.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Background checks; Staff; I-9 and background check requirements by worker type; U.S. Department of Labor, Fair Labor Standards Act

entries.title: Converting a pending worker
entries.body: Convert the day clear to start arrives, so the business unit approver, PCB, and central HR can approve the hire before day one. Use Convert, never Quick Convert or Edit Pending Worker, and make every change inside it. A paid hire gets Hire employment, Active payroll eligible, and a place on the new hire report. Payroll details follow the worker: monthly (regular) salary for exempt staff, and weekly or biweekly hourly pay with a time card required for non-exempt staff. Payroll can only pay what your hire record says.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Convert a pending worker; The HCM's role in payroll

entries.title: New position or update?
entries.body: A new role gets a new position. Don't reactivate an inactive position, because old job codes on it can block approval, and don't repurpose a vacant position built for another worker type. When the same role changes, such as a reclass, update its position with Compensation's reclass memo attached. After approval, person type, location, working hours, and hourly salary don't sync to the person's assignment, so update those with Change Assignment.
entries.source: HCM Academy: When to create a new position vs. update an existing position; Update a position

entries.title: The pre-search memo comes first
entries.body: Before you create a staff or non-exempt position, get Compensation's pre-search memo through your EC. Send the position description and the real work location. The memo gives the six-digit job code, the job name and level, the assignment category, and the pay range. Central HR approves the position only with the memo attached. Central recruiting checks that the requisition's memo is less than 12 months old and has the same job code.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Compensation Management: Getting the Compensation Memo; Job Architecture overview and how it impacts recruiting decisions

entries.title: Position fields that get sent back
entries.body: Effective date: today, not the start date, so the position can be approved and posted. Standard working hours: always 40, with the actual hours in Working hours (30 of 40 is an FTE of 0.75). Job: the six-digit code from the memo, never a retired four- or five-digit code. Manager: blank, because the manager belongs on the assignment. Location: the real site. Attach the memo and the position description.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Create a position; Position management best practices

entries.title: Requisition settings
entries.body: The requisition copies the position when you submit it and never syncs, so fix the position first. Openings: Limited, with the exact number of seats, never Unlimited, because every opening is billed and canceling unfilled ones costs half the fee. Location: the specific site, never United States, because location decides whether the posting must show a pay range. The requisition title is only the posting title; the new hire's business title is the job name.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Create a requisition; Job Architecture overview and how it impacts recruiting decisions

entries.title: Non-workers
entries.body: Someone who needs access but won't be paid is a non-worker: the Non-employment hire reason, Active no payroll, and excluded from the new hire report. Campus affiliates need a background check but not an I-9. Never use Active no payroll for anyone who should be paid, because they won't be.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Non-Workers

entries.title: Paid and unpaid interns
entries.body: A paid intern is an employee, hired for their worker type. An unpaid internship is allowed only when the intern, not the office, is the primary beneficiary. An intern doing regular work the office would otherwise pay for is likely an employee, owed at least minimum wage and overtime. A signed waiver doesn't change that, and no single factor, such as course credit, decides it. When it's unclear, treat it as paid and talk with your EC before the start date. [SME] Which worker type and category Vanderbilt uses for interns, and which checks apply.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Interns (Paid and Unpaid); U.S. Department of Labor, Fact Sheet #71

entries.title: Rehires
entries.body: A former employee's eligibility comes from the rehire recommendation set when they were terminated. If it says No, stop and talk with the recruiter and your EC before anyone makes an offer. Never edit the field to get around it, and never create a second person record: a rehire adds a new work relationship to the existing record. [SME] Who can approve rehiring someone marked No, and how Not specified is handled.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Rehires and eligibility for rehire

entries.title: Union-covered positions
entries.body: When a collective bargaining agreement covers a position, the agreement sets starting pay, steps, and probation. Don't negotiate outside it or change its terms on your own, even to pay more. Confirm coverage with your EC before you post, and route any exception through them. [SME] Which positions are union-covered, where the agreements are kept, and how they show in Oracle.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Union Employees

entries.title: Executive and outside searches
entries.body: Most staff searches run through central recruiting and its recruiting partner. The partner's own executive search program uses a recruiting requisition with the Executive search type. Any other search firm is paid through a PO requisition with your procurement contact, not a recruiting requisition. Confirm with central recruiting before an executive search starts.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Executive or External Search

entries.title: Pay ranges in postings
entries.body: Vanderbilt posts a pay range only where the law requires it: New York and California. The location on the position flows to the requisition and the posting, so it must name the real place, never United States. A job worked in New York, or reporting to a supervisor there, needs the range. New York requisitions also use the New York candidate selection process. [SME] How postings open to several locations or remote anywhere are handled.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Pay transparency; Create a requisition

entries.title: Work in another state
entries.body: When someone will work from another state, that state's rules can apply: tax withholding and registration, unemployment insurance, workers' compensation, pay frequency, and wage and leave laws. Get the work state and date in writing and flag it to your EC before the offer or the move. The assignment location is where the person actually works, effective the day they start working there. [SME] Vanderbilt's Out of State Risk Assessment form and process, who owns each review area, and the lead time for a new state.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Out of State Risk Assessment

entries.title: State pay and leave rules
entries.body: Each state sets how often employees must be paid, and some states and cities add sick and family leave rules beyond federal law. These follow where the person works, so the work location on the assignment must be right. Check pay frequency with payroll before an offer or a move, and route state leave questions to your EC. You don't administer state leave programs. [SME] How Vanderbilt pays and tracks leave for staff who work in other states.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Payroll cadence; Regional benefits and leave

entries.title: FMLA basics: route it the same day
entries.body: FMLA gives eligible employees up to 12 workweeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period for qualifying reasons, such as caring for a parent with a serious health condition. Once the office learns an employee may need leave for an FMLA reason, the employer must give the eligibility notice within 5 business days, so get the leave need to the leave team the same day. Don't ask for a diagnosis or decide eligibility yourself; the leave team handles eligibility and medical certification. Tell the manager what they need to plan, such as dates, and keep medical details private. [SME] Confirm how HCMs hand a leave need to the Vanderbilt leave team and who sends the eligibility notice.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Entering and managing FMLA/TMLA transactions; U.S. Department of Labor, Family and Medical Leave Act

entries.title: Continuous or intermittent leave
entries.body: Continuous leave is one block of time off, entered as one absence with start and end dates. Intermittent leave is separate blocks of time for one reason, and a reduced schedule is fewer hours per day or week. For those, record each occurrence with the actual time taken, as it happens, because only time actually taken counts against the 12 weeks. Never book an intermittent approval as one long block. File the approval letter as a Document Record of type Leave and Accommodation Documentation. [SME] Confirm which absence types Vanderbilt uses for FMLA and TMLA, who enters intermittent occurrences, and whether a biweekly employee's protected leave goes on the time card system, in Oracle absences, or both.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Entering and managing FMLA/TMLA transactions

entries.title: Exempt time off lives in Oracle
entries.body: Exempt (monthly) employees' time off is recorded in Oracle absences, not the time card system. Non-exempt (weekly and biweekly) time off goes on the time card system with a pay code. Before you enter exempt time off, check Absence Balance and Existing Absences, then use Add Absence with the right type and dates. To fix a mistake, edit or withdraw the absence on file; never enter a second one. Get it approved before the monthly cutoff on the payroll calendar. [SME] Confirm whether HCMs can approve exempt time off or only managers can, and confirm the 2026 monthly cutoff dates.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Managing Exempt Time Off in Oracle; Differences in processing leaves for monthly vs. biweekly employees

entries.title: Leave approvals and statuses
entries.body: A submitted absence goes to approval, by default to the employee's line manager. Awaiting approval means it's still with an approver and hasn't reached payroll. Scheduled means approved for a future date, and Completed means approved and past. Track it with the notifications bell and chase approvers well before the payroll cutoff. To cancel an approved absence, withdraw it; it shows Awaiting withdrawal approval until the withdrawal is approved, then Withdrawn. [SME] Confirm Vanderbilt's approval routing for each absence type, including whether the leave team is in the chain.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Leave administration workflows within Oracle

entries.title: Leave status on the assignment
entries.body: The assignment status tells HR and payroll whether someone is working or on leave. It is separate from the absence record: changing one does not change the other, so check both. When a leave starts, changes, or ends, run Change Assignment with the leave status action, effective the date it actually happens (for a return, the first day back), and confirm it in Employment Info. This applies to every employee, exempt or not, because the assignment lives in Oracle. [SME] Confirm the exact leave status action and status names Vanderbilt uses, including the return to work status.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Leave status updates; Change Assignment

entries.title: Which student setup?
entries.body: Pick the setup before you enter anything. A student who works for pay is a student worker: hire reason Hire employment, status Active payroll eligible, an I-9 but no background check, and pay from approved time cards. A student who gets a stipend and performs no services is a service free stipend: hire reason Service free appointment, with no I-9 and no background check. A student who only needs expenses paid back is Student Expense Only, with no I-9 and no background check. Never pay for work with a gift card, invoice, stipend, or reimbursement. [SME] Confirm the Oracle setup for stipends and expense only records, who confirms student eligibility, and how to date a hire and pay hours a student worked before being hired.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Student hiring process and requirements; Student Workers; Service Free Stipend; Student Expense Only

entries.title: Add a Work Relationship or an assignment?
entries.body: Search the person in Employment Info first; Oracle keeps one person record and adds to it. If the student has only an enrolled student (N) record, add the employment Work Relationship. If the student already has an employee (E) assignment, add an assignment. Never create a second person record. [SME] Confirm the exact Quick Action names Vanderbilt uses for these two actions.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Add a Work Relationship or add an Assignment?

entries.title: End student jobs on time
entries.body: When a term or work period ends, end the assignment so the student isn't left active and payable. Use End Assignment in Change Assignment, dated the last day of the term or work period. End Assignment stops one job; Terminate Employment ends every job in the work relationship, so never terminate someone who keeps another job. [SME] Confirm Vanderbilt's term change calendar, whether student assignments are ended in bulk, and which End Assignment entry point to use.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Student and faculty assignment changes; Ending assignments vs. terminating employment

entries.title: Track student and faculty approvals
entries.body: Student and faculty transactions go to approval before they take effect. Track yours with the notifications bell; its approval history shows who it's waiting on. If one is stuck, contact that approver before the cutoff, or your EC if you can't tell who holds it. To fix a pending transaction, withdraw it, correct it, and resubmit; never submit a duplicate. [SME] Confirm Vanderbilt's approval routing for student and faculty transactions.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Oracle transactions and approvals for these populations; HCM Workflow and Worklists

entries.title: Faculty pay isn't staff pay
entries.body: Staff supplements are not for faculty, post-docs, students, or temps. Faculty have their own supplements, and faculty pay costs to its own element account (5110), not staff (5120) or student (5130). Faculty are exempt and paid monthly, so pay approved after the monthly cutoff waits for the next month. [SME] Confirm which faculty supplement elements Vanderbilt uses, who approves and enters them, and the faculty and staff account numbers.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Faculty; Add a staff supplement

entries.title: Faculty hires: both checks first
entries.body: Faculty need an I-9 and a background check, the same as staff. Don't let a faculty member start before PCB emails clear to start; then convert with hire reason Hire employment and status Active payroll eligible. I-9 Section 1 is due by the first day of work and Section 2 within 3 business days. [SME] Confirm whether faculty hires come through a requisition or a manual background check request, and the role of faculty affairs in appointments.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Faculty hiring process and requirements; I-9 and background check requirements by worker type

entries.title: Emeritus and FERDC: confirm first
entries.body: Vanderbilt's Oracle setup for emeritus and FERDC appointments is still being confirmed, including worker type, hire reason, status, position, and who approves. Until it is, don't enter anything. Search the person in Employment Info, then confirm the setup with your EC. Never reactivate an inactive position, reuse a position across worker types, or copy a similar record's setup. [SME] Confirm the emeritus and FERDC setups, what FERDC covers, and who owns each.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Emeritus; FERDC

entries.title: Changing someone's working hours
entries.body: When hours change, use Change Assignment with Salary selected, so hours and pay change in one transaction. Enter the new working hours and leave standard working hours at 40; FTE recalculates (30 of 40 is 0.75). Check the salary step against what was agreed, and attach the approval. Change Salary with the reason Change in working hours changes only the salary, not the hours. For biweekly staff, start the change on the first day of a pay period, and have it entered and approved by the HCM transaction cutoff.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Change Working Hours; Change Assignment

entries.title: Transfers and promotions from a requisition
entries.body: When an employee applies for a posted job and accepts it, the transfer or promotion is submitted centrally (in this office, through central recruiting) and then routed to your business unit's approvers. HCMs do not submit these, because that access would expose every business unit's transfers. Do not create a direct hire for someone already in process, and do not end or terminate the old job: the transfer moves the assignment. Stay in touch with the recruiter, and ask central recruiting before you act if a start date is close and you cannot find the person.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Transfer or promotion from a requisition; Promote

entries.title: Moves inside your business unit
entries.body: With no requisition, the HCM in the employee's current business unit submits the move with Transfer: an organization transfer for a planned move inside the business unit, or a transfer to faculty status. Do not change someone's position with Change Assignment. Positions cannot move between business units. If pay type changes, select Payroll details; moving an hourly biweekly employee to monthly takes effect the day after a biweekly pay period ends. Promote without a requisition is also yours to submit. Ask your EC whether an internal posting rule applies [SME].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Transfer or promotion without a requisition; Promote

entries.title: End Assignment or Terminate Employment
entries.body: End Assignment stops one job; the work relationship and any other jobs keep going. Terminate Employment ends the work relationship and every assignment in it, including jobs in other areas, and stops their pay. Oracle will not end someone's only assignment (terminate instead) or their primary assignment (make the job they keep primary first). Before you submit, list every assignment and talk with the HCM who owns the other job: agree on the dates and on who submits what [SME].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Ending assignments vs. terminating employment; How to handle a termination when an employee has multiple assignments

entries.title: Offboarding checklist
entries.body: Check for other assignments and end only your job if the person keeps one. Move any direct reports before the end date. Enter the dates, revoke access After termination (standard), and leave payroll eligibility as defaulted. The transaction stops pay and payroll works from the record, so there is no separate payroll step. Non-exempt staff need a final approved time card; exempt staff have none. Review costing on the ending assignment, file final documents as Document Records, and close out equipment and the exit survey [SME: owners]. Submit before the payroll cutoff on the worker's calendar.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Offboarding process requirements

entries.title: Resignations, misconduct, and reductions in force
entries.body: Resignation: Voluntary separation, reason Resigned. The notification date is the day the employee told the manager, and the termination date is the actual last day (replace any date Oracle fills in). Misconduct: talk with your EC and leadership first, and settle when access ends and how the rehire field is marked [SME: field name]; then Involuntary termination, reason Misconduct. Reduction in force: 60 days' notice from the notification date, the termination date is the end of the notice, and the separation agreement decides working or non-working notice. In every case, leave payroll eligibility as defaulted.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Voluntary termination; Involuntary termination (misconduct); Reduction in force (RIF)

entries.title: Moving a manager's team
entries.body: Use Direct Reports on the departing manager's record to move the whole team in one transaction, effective on or before the manager's last day. Use Change Manager when only one person needs a new manager. Move reports before you end the manager's job, so approvals and time card sign off never land on someone who is gone. Large teams move in batches of up to 50. Confirm the new manager's approver setup with your EC [SME].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Direct Reports

entries.title: A second job for a current employee
entries.body: If the person already has an employee assignment, use Add Assignment. The new job gets its own position, hours, pay, manager, and costing; the existing job keeps its salary and stays primary unless the new job becomes the main one. Point the new assignment at an active position with the right job code. Ask your EC about action reasons and any pre-approval a second job needs [SME].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Add Assignment

entries.title: How costing works
entries.body: Costing decides which accounts pay for a person's pay. Oracle uses the most specific level it finds: element, then assignment, then the work unit default. Blank costing is not an error; it charges the work unit default (program 000 if your department splits by program). Split funding needs one line per source, totaling 100%, because Vanderbilt's setup will not send a remainder to a default. Costing applies to the whole pay period, using what is in effect on the period end date. In this office you enter costing in Costing for Persons with the strings Mei sends. Oracle does not check the strings and there is no approval step, so run the HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan report after you submit.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Costing fundamentals; Enter costing for a person

entries.title: Changing costing that already exists
entries.body: Check History first. Update starts different costing as of a date (search on the first day of the pay period it starts). Correct revises a record for its whole date range (search on the first day of the period it should have started). End Date stops costing (search on the last day of the last pay period it should apply), and it ends everything from that date forward. Delete Record removes a record completely. After an End Date, use Create to add costing again. Action labels come from a training guide that predates the current screens [SME].
entries.source: HCM Academy: Change existing costing

entries.title: Fixing costing for periods already paid
entries.body: Current and future costing changes must be in by the HCM transaction cutoff. Any change that reaches a period already paid also needs the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary), sent to Research Finance by the Retro Change Cutoff (Wed Oct 21 for this period) [SME], with the costing entered as it should have been. Add a cost transfer memo if an externally funded grant is affected. Late fixes add work for payroll and finance, so catch errors before the cutoff.
entries.source: HCM Academy: Enter costing for a person; How employee costing impacts payroll and financial reporting

entries.title: Costing when someone changes business units
entries.body: Costing follows an employee who changes business units; it does not reset. Review it on every transfer. If the new area uses its default, End Date the old costing on the last day of the last pay period it should apply. If it needs specific costing, Update it from the first day of the pay period the transfer takes effect. Tell the other HCM what you changed [SME: which HCM owns this step].
